Scientific name: Corymbophanes andersoni Eigenmann, 1909.

Type locality: Aruataima Falls, Upper Potaro R., Guyana, 5°00'05''N, 59°37'33''W.

Etymology: (Greek) Korymbos = summit, cluster of fruit or flowers + (Greek) phaino = to shine.

Size: 86 mm SL (8.6 cm).
South America: Essequibo River drainage, upper Potaro River, upstream of Kaieteur Falls.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Distinguished from C. kaiei by having the abdomen lightly colored, caudal fin without light bands, anal fin I,4, caudal peduncle strongly compressed, and 5 plates below adpressed pectoral fin spine. Generic characteristics: caudal fin 1, 14, 1; adipose fin replaced by low elongate postdorsal ridge formed by series of raised median unpaired plates contiguous with dorsal procurrent caudal fin spines.
